questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- the high global rank of the University of Washington
- the research opportunities at the University of Washington
- the opportunity to interact with the US culture as a whole and visit various places across US

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The accommodation upon arrival process was smooth and the administrative staff and fellow colleagues were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- someone was waiting for us in the parking lot to help us find our dorm room
- there were various meetings for international students were I was able to meet other exchange students and find out useful information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Me and my friend (both KU exchange students) were assigned a shared dorm room and a shared bathroom. The bathroom was shared with 8 other people

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We were forced to buy an expensive meal plan in the campus and the food quality was low.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is very expensive (prepare to spend ~1500 USD on food and housing) and given the fact that 99% you will receive a shared room (except the case when you need some special accommodation) and you will be forced to eat in campus, I would say that you should consider very well if you are willing to spend the next two quarters under these circumstances

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very hard to register to the desired subjects at the University of Washington. As an exchange student, I was considered university-wide exchange student so I had no major (even if at KU, I am Computer Science Master student). 80% of the classes are majors only, so if you don't have any major you can apply for a class but you will have lower priority and since Computer Science is a very competitive subject at UW, me and my friend were able to get into only one Computer Science class. The other two classes we got into were some generic first or second year subjects (one was Leadership) which were going to be very dull and boring.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administrative people were very helpful as much as they could, but since we had no major it was very hard for us to get into any kind of classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Me and my friend got extremely lucky because I have received an email from a UW computer science professor in which he was advertising a research project. Since we had a couple of years working as professional ML engineers, we were able to get into this research project for which we have received a lot of credits (17 UW credits = ~22 ECTS). Given this, we could drop most of the useless classes that we got into and work on the research project.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you just want to spend one or two quarters at a US university, I would say that UW is way to expensive and very hard to find classes (you can get on some first year generic economics classes or leadership which are totally useless). 
If you want to get into top of the world research and have a chance of publishing into an international journal, UW is your chance. I would totally advise master students that want to go for an exchange at UW to directly write emails to teachers and ask them for temporary research positions in the laboratories they lead. If there is someone interested in computer science/machine learning research, they can contact me on linked-in (username: "Filip Tasadan") and I can help them with useful advices and even direct them to some of the laboratories that I have collaborated with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had taken only two classes (since I was mostly doing research). One class was first year (bachelors) leadership, which was quite boring but I was able to talk to some students that otherwise I would have never met. Since the leadership class had a lot of social activities (group projects, group discussions, etc.) it was very easy to talk to other people that had very different majors (it was a non-major class).
The other class was Introduction to Human Computer Interaction, which was one of the best university classes I have ever attended. The level of commitment from the teacher and TAs was incredible, and the subjects presented were very actual. The HCI class has broadened my perspective on human centered design, and I am very satisfied that I have attended this class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more focused on the student and there were more discussions between us and the teachers compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At UW there is the Intramural Activities Building (IMA) which has all the imaginable sports (from athletics at the top floor with the view of the bay to basketball, volleyball, soccer, gym, swimming pool) and for each sport there a a lot of classes that you can take. There is even a sauna. I was spending my evenings and weekends there either in the gym or at some class (classes are very cheap, around 10$ / class).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- search of the UW hiking club, they have 1 or 2 activates every weekend and it's a very nice way to meet people and explore the Washington state
- there are ethnic clubs (I was able to find a Romanian club) in which you can meet very nice people and go to parties together

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would explore as much as possible of the US if you have the money to do it. Below I will list some of the places that I liked the most:
- Vancouver, Canada (you can go by bus, 3h from Seattle)
- Las Vegas, Nevada (you must rent a car and go into the desert and at Hoover dam, it's an incredible experience)
- San Francisco, California (it is 20% more expensive than Seattle but I would go anytime again there for a long weekend)
- Austin, Texas (vibrant city with a lot of social activates)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, Americans are great at feeling everyone welcomed and they are very helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were no particular cultural differences that I have found challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and helpfulness of the people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- plan your budget very carefully and make sure you have all the money to cover any emergencies
- try to get in touch to teachers directly through email or go and knock on their office. Most of them are going to be helpful and try to help you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing top level research which colleagues from all over the world (China, Middle East, India) into one of the best NLP laboratories in the US.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The housing and food, I was barely coping with the low quality of both the living space and of everyday meals.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
